Consider the functions f(x) = 1/(x − 4) + 1, for x ≠ 4, and g(x) = x − 3, for x ∈ ℝ.

The following diagram shows the graphs of f and g.

[Diagram: Coordinate axes labelled x and y. The graph y = f has two decreasing branches separated by the vertical asymptote x = 4 and tending to the horizontal asymptote y = 1: its left branch crosses the x-axis at A, and its upper-right branch intersects the increasing straight line y = g at B. The straight line also passes through A.]

The graphs of f and g intersect at points A and B. The coordinates of A are (3, 0).

(a) Find the coordinates of B. [5]

In the following diagram, the shaded region is enclosed by the graph of f, the graph of g, the x-axis, and the line x = k, where k ∈ ℤ.

[Diagram: The same graphs are shown with a vertical line x = k to the right of B. The shaded region lies above the x-axis. From A to B it is bounded above by the line g; from B to x = k it is bounded above by the upper-right branch of f. Its right boundary is the vertical line x = k.]

The area of the shaded region can be written as ln(p) + 8, where p ∈ ℤ.

records.independentSolutionText: (a) 1/(x−4)+1=x−3 gives (x−3)(x−5)=0; hence B=(5,2). (b) Splitting the shown region at x=5, use ∫f dx=ln|x−4|+x and the triangular line area. The combined area simplifies to ln(k−4)+k−3. Equating with ln p+8 gives k=11 and p=7.

Graphs of f and g are shown. f is linear with x-intercept (6, 0) and y-intercept (0, 12). g has x-intercepts (−2, 0), (6, 0) and y-intercept (0, 12).

[Diagram: a descending line through (0, 12) and (6, 0), and a downward parabola through all three stated intercepts; the parabola is above the line between x=0 and x=6.]

(a) Write f(x)=mx+c. [2]

g(x)=−x²+bx+12.

(b) Find b. [3]

(c) Show that the enclosed area is ∫₀⁶(−x² + 6x) dx. [2]

(d) Hence find the area. [4]

At P on g, the tangent is parallel to f.

(e) Find P. [5]
records.independentSolutionText: (a) Slope=−2, so f(x)=−2x + 12. (b) Substitution of (6,0) gives b=4. (c) g−f=−x² + 6x, so area=∫₀⁶(−x² + 6x) dx. (d) Integrating gives 36 square units. (e) g′(x)=−2x+4; equate to −2 and substitute in g, giving P=(3, 15).

5. [Maximum mark: 8]

The following diagram shows the graph of y = (Ax + B)/(x − 4), where x ∈ ℝ, x ≠ 4 and A, B ∈ ℤ.

The graph passes through the points P(−10, 1) and Q(3, −12).

[Coordinate diagram: a reciprocal-type graph has vertical asymptote x = 4 and horizontal asymptote y = 2. Its left branch passes through P(−10, 1), crosses the x-axis to the left of the y-axis, passes below the y-axis and through Q(3, −12), then tends downward as x approaches 4 from the left. Its right branch tends upward as x approaches 4 from the right and approaches y = 2 from above as x increases.]

(a) Determine the value of A and the value of B. [3]

(b) Describe a sequence of transformations that would map the graph of y = 1/x onto the graph of y = (Ax + B)/(x − 4). [5]
records.independentSolutionText:
(a) Substituting P(−10, 1) into y = (Ax + B)/(x − 4) gives 1 = (−10A + B)/(−14), so −10A + B = −14. Substituting Q(3, −12) gives −12 = (3A + B)/(−1), so 3A + B = 12. Subtracting the first equation from the second gives 13A = 26, hence A = 2. Then 3(2) + B = 12, so B = 6.

(b) With A = 2 and B = 6, y = (2x + 6)/(x − 4) = 2 + 14/(x − 4). Starting from y = 1/x: apply a vertical stretch by scale factor 14; translate 4 units to the right; then translate 2 units upwards. The horizontal translation may be performed before or after the vertical stretch, but the vertical stretch must precede the upward translation.
